title: Legacy ChatCompletions compatibility proxy for client SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a backward-compatibility proxy layer that accepts legacy OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request/response shapes from older client SDKs and maps them to Redwood's canonical chat API and runtime. The proxy should preserve streaming semantics (SSE/Chunked), map function/tool calling shapes to Redwood tool hooks, support structured output validation, and translate errors/usage telemetry back to the old client surface so that existing customers and partners can upgrade without changing SDKs immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts legacy ChatCompletions JSON (messages, max_tokens, temperature, stop) and forwards equivalent requests to Redwood runtime with canonical chat payload.
Streaming responses from Redwood (token deltas, function call chunks, structured output blocks) are re-encoded as OpenAI-style chunked SSE stream frames expected by older SDKs.
Function/tool calling: map Redwood tool invocation events to 'finish_reason: "function_call"' and payload shape matching legacy 'message' with name/content fields.
Request/response idempotency headers and request ids are preserved and surfaced in legacy response metadata and logs.
End-to-end telemetry uses existing usage counters so customers see per-token billing roughly matching pre-proxy behavior (within <2% variance for canonical workloads).

Automated integration tests cover 1) non-streaming text-only paths, 2) streaming with SSE reconnection, 3) tool calling with multi-part function arguments, 4) structured output schema enforcement failures and fallbacks.
Rollback plan and canary gating are defined and verified in staging before production rollout.
implementation_notes: Create a lightweight HTTP proxy service (cc-compat-proxy) that lives in edge cluster and can be toggled per-tenant via routing policy.

Request mapping: normalize legacy 'messages' -> canonical 'conversation' format; map role aliases (assistant/system/user) and convert content types (delta events vs full content) into same internal deltas format.

Streaming: support both server-sent events (text/event-stream) and chunked JSON; implement buffer/windowing to re-emit Redwood token deltas as OpenAI-style 'data: [JSON]

' chunks without violating latency SLOs.

Function/Tool calling: when Redwood emits a tool-invoke event, synthesize an incremental stream where the final frame contains 'finish_reason: "function_call"' and the function payload serialized to the legacy single-message content field. Also support legacy two-phase function streams where name arrives first and payload streamed afterwards.

Structured output: run canonical JSON schema validator on generated output; when schema mismatch occurs, emit a legacy-compatible fallback text chunk and surface a structured_error field in response headers for partner diagnostics.
Telemetry: attach original client headers (X-Request-ID, X-SDK-Version) to internal traces; translate runtime latency/cost into legacy usage headers so downstream dashboards remain accurate.
Error mapping: translate Redwood error codes to legacy OpenAI-like codes (e.g., rate_limit -> 429 with 'rate_limit_exceeded' string) and preserve human-readable message.
Security: proxy must strip-internal-only headers and enforce RBAC/AAD checks identical to Redwood frontdoor; no secret material persisted in logs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff — scoped features and acceptance criteria with PM and DS. Agreed to support SSE and chunked responses parallelly.
2025-02-22: Prototype streaming shim completed — emits OpenAI-style SSE frames from canonical delta stream. Latency tests: median added latency ~8ms per chunk in staging.
2025-02-25: Design review with Security — confirmed header stripping rules and required per-tenant opt-in for Private deployments.
2025-02-27: Implemented function-call finalization mapping; edge cases for streamed function args identified (large payload chunking).
2025-03-01: Integration tests added for schema validation fallback; found inconsistency in how legacy SDKs expect content quoting — added escaping step.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Kapoor): Ensure telemetry mapping doesn't under-report token usage for billing reconciliations.
Design (Sofia Martinez): Recommend adding a header X-Compat-Mode with reason code to help partner support identify proxied requests.
Security (Anya Petrov): Confirmed that proxy cannot be used to bypass tenant network restrictions — added mandatory tenancy header check.
Infra (Ben Liu): Suggest autoscaling policy that follows spike patterns from legacy SDKs which tend to open many short-lived streaming connections.
tests: Integration test: legacy client -> proxy -> runtime non-streaming path validated with golden response comparison
Integration test: legacy SSE client disconnect/reconnect behavior reproduces expected idempotent resume semantics
Property test: token accounting between legacy headers and runtime metrics within 2% across sampled prompts
End-to-end test: function calling where tool returns multipart JSON and proxy reassembles into single legacy message
canary_plan: Stage: deploy to canary cluster and enable for 3 internal tenants for 48 hours. Metrics: error_rate < 0.5%, 95p latency uplift < 15%, token-accounting variance < 2%. Ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 60% over 8 hours if metrics stable.
rollback_plan: Toggle routing via service mesh flag to bypass cc-compat-proxy if error_rate or cost regression observed. Revert to prior routing within 15 minutes; run postmortem and patch before next attempt.
notes: Avoid adding new breaking translations — this proxy is intended as temporary compatibility surface until customers migrate SDKs.
We will deprecate support for very old SDK versions after usage falls below 1% for 30 days.
